method: Read all six requested files and exact diffs from HEAD bce674a; traced active recovery callers rather than treating display history as an active receipt store.
Independently reported the accepted-record capacity regression before the final repair; retained the initial finding unchanged and reviewed the repair/new tests.
Checked imported helpers, mutation/reconciliation consumers, typed terminal/emergency owner payload, exact draft revision cleanup and legacy migration semantics.
Did not execute tests or change product source; parsed the author final raw JSON/log rather than assuming the pending test run passed.

checks.conclusion: Display metadata retains newest 500 closed rows by createdAt with deterministic ID tie break; active records retain an independent 200 cap plus one explicit emergency slot. Active count, not history size, drives admission. GC moves eligible rows from active to display history in one transaction.

Normal API acceptance still auto-acknowledges ordinary methods. Reconciliation retains immediate proof; later pressure GC can collect ordinary accepted rows. INPUT/fork/convert/review destination receipts remain until the destination has actually loaded; terminal/open and system/recover remain for their typed owners.

A matching loaded legacy destination can now become consumed and later archived, while both update and consumption skip legacy draft clearing. Unseen legacy destinations remain active. Already acknowledged malformed legacy records only set a history warning, preserving the prior migration admission behavior.

History append and active deletion share the strict readwrite operations+meta IDB transaction. Failed writes/abort leave the active row. Invalid history containers/rows are ignored with a display warning; malformed active records still fail closed. Full IDB storage failure is not claimed recoverable.

Accepted draft cleanup remains exact revision scoped; not_sent/unknown/legacy closure does not clear the unsent draft. Absent active rows are not recreated by late update/reconciliation; closed IDs still present in retained history cannot be allocated again. History is a bounded display archive, not an unbounded ID tombstone store.

Existing shared IDB serialization and BroadcastChannel/storage/focus notifications remain in use. Each hook rejects disposed/older read results; history and active rows are read in one snapshot with active-ID deduplication. No separate best-effort history write was introduced.

Dedicated history includes all retained active+closed records newest first with full local dates. Closed unknown rows retain the unknown fact but have no query, retire or stop controls; normal accepted records need no second confirmation. Pending/unknown query, not_received fencing and proof-bound stop remain. Inline not_sent dismissal remains available and now archives its row. The obsolete showCompleted flag/manual bulk cleanup state is removed.

Closed history keeps method, IDs, time, state and closure category; it omits draft identities, terminal leases/results, recovery lists, resource paths and request/result/error bodies. Live failure reasons remain on-demand and transient.

resolvedFindings.title: Queried accepted non-thread operations lose their last active-budget release path
resolvedFindings.suggestedBoundary: Add safe automatic collection eligibility for accepted receipts that require no further owner handoff; keep terminal/recovery owner payload and unseen thread destinations until consumed. Do not immediately erase the proof before useWorkflow observers can read it; do not clear legacy/unsent/newer drafts.
resolvedFindings.validation: Static end-to-end caller proof only; no new test or runtime reproduction performed by this reviewer.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Pressure GC now collects ordinary accepted receipts; legacy destination consumption is allowed without draft cleanup; terminal and emergency owner proofs are excluded. New targeted cases cover 240 queried/legacy ordinary rows, destination-bound legacy collection with original draft, and retained terminal/emergency owner payload.
